I found three bugs in the uncommitted changes. I only read the diff and the full `shouldBypassProxy.js`. I didn't run the code or the tests, and I didn't read the test diffs.

1. **`lib/helpers/shouldBypassProxy.js:108`: NO_PROXY now matches hosts it never listed.**
   - The new check `isLoopback(hostname) && isLoopback(entryHost)` treats `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1` as the same host.
   - With `NO_PROXY=localhost`, a request to `http://127.0.0.1` or `http://[::1]` now skips the proxy. Before, it went through the proxy.
   - Users who list only one loopback name, for example to proxy `127.0.0.1` through a local tunnel, will have those requests sent directly.
   - Only exact names in `NO_PROXY` should match. If the aliasing is intended, it should be opt-in.
   - The check also has no port logic of its own, so it relies on the earlier port check.
   - `127.0.0.2` through `127.255.255.255` are loopback too, but the set doesn't cover them. The behavior is inconsistent as well as too broad.

2. **`lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js:~14, 50`: header values with CR/LF are now silently altered instead of rejected.**
   - `assertValidHeaderValue` was removed, so `"a\r\nb"` becomes `"ab"` with no error.
   - Callers who relied on the `Invalid character in header content` error to catch bad input no longer get it. Their data is quietly rewritten.
   - Injection is still blocked, but the rejection is gone.

3. **`lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js:8`: the sanitizer strips every character above `\xFF`.**
   - The regex `/[^\x09\x20-\x7E\x80-\xFF]/g` removes all of them without warning. That includes emoji and CJK text, and `\x7F` and other control characters go the same way.
   - A value like `"名前"` becomes `""`. The header is then sent empty, or with fragments of the original value, and nothing reports it.
   - Node's `http` would have thrown on these characters, so this hides a real error.
   - Values are also now trimmed of leading and trailing spaces and tabs, which is a new behavior. Whitespace-only values become `""`.
